mechanism_narrative: RETAIL_REC has declined in each of the last four weekly means, from 3.7 to -13.3, and this downward momentum persists because households and businesses do not fully adjust spending and staffing within one week, so the next 28-day mean is below the last 28-day mean.
failure_condition: The mean of RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is greater than or equal to its mean over the last 28 days.

mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT mobility has fallen below -8 percent from baseline, a threshold that in prior tightening phases signals sharply reduced trips into commercial districts; once crossed, retail and recreation visits continue to fall over the following two weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT weekly mean falls below -8 percent change from baseline
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is not lower than over the last 28 days when TRANSIT is below -8.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneously weak PARKS and non-positive WORKPLACES indicate that both discretionary outdoor leisure and office commuting are suppressed; the interaction of these two channels amplifies the decline in RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: When PARKS < -10 and WORKPLACES <= 0, the next 28-day mean of RETAIL_REC is higher than or equal to the last 28-day mean.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM has stayed above 45 for four consecutive weekly means, indicating essential-only shopping and precautionary stockpiling; this behavior crowds out discretionary retail trips and pushes RETAIL_REC lower over the next week.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM remains above 45 for at least two consecutive weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 7 days is higher than its value at t-0w while GROCERY_PHARM remains above 45.

mechanism_narrative: RESIDENTIAL has risen from 4.9 to 9.3 percent above baseline, meaning more people are staying home; elevated residential time mechanically reduces out-of-home retail and recreation visits, so RETAIL_REC continues falling over the next two weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is higher than over the last 28 days while RESIDENTIAL remains above 8.

mechanism_narrative: PARKS has fallen to -16.7, consistent with seasonal winter constraints; as the season transitions, a PARKS recovery above -10 releases pent-up outdoor and adjacent retail demand, driving RETAIL_REC higher over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS rises above -10 percent change from baseline
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not rise above its last 28-day mean within four weeks after PARKS rises above -10.

mechanism_narrative: WORKPLACES rebounded to +6.0 at t-1w before falling to -0.6 at t-0w; if WORKPLACES stays positive for two consecutive weeks, commuting and office-adjacent spending return, lifting RETAIL_REC over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES weekly mean > 0 for two consecutive weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is not higher than over the last 28 days when WORKPLACES has been positive for two consecutive weeks.

mechanism_narrative: Deeply negative PARKS and TRANSIT together with high RESIDENTIAL indicate a broad withdrawal from public spaces; this three-way mobility pattern suppresses retail and recreation visits over the next week more than any single series would predict.
failure_condition: When PARKS < -10, TRANSIT < -5, and RESIDENTIAL > 8, RETAIL_REC over the next 7 days is higher than or equal to its t-0w level.
